{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVRkquM8AAAABZgg4lw", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn_T5zhDHnf0", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn_T5", "number": 57, "title": "Resolve and implement non-interlaced OBJ evaluation limits and STAT77 overflow reporting", "body": "## Problem

OBJ evaluation currently applies incomplete limits and cannot report overflow to software. This is the next incomplete behavior identified by the latest assessment, following Issue #55’s rectangular geometry implementation. The supplied context lists no open Issue covering it.

At baseline `a7d944c662b1bbfca3ed9856240f7b9660c7bc56`:

- [`Ppu::objects`](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/a7d944c662b1bbfca3ed9856240f7b9660c7bc56/crates/snes-core/src/ppu.rs#L578) increments its object count using vertical inclusion alone, before considering horizontal position. Selection, tile budgeting and pixel composition share one traversal.
- Tile counting occurs after per-pixel clipping, only where `col & 7 == 0`. A partially visible tile whose first pixel is offscreen can escape counting. Exceeding the budget breaks only the current object’s pixel loop.
- [`Ppu::read($213E)`](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/a7d944c662b1bbfca3ed9856240f7b9660c7bc56/crates/snes-core/src/ppu.rs#L334) returns `(open1 & $10) | $01`, with no overflow state.
- Existing [OBJ geometry tests](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/a7d944c662b1bbfca3ed9856240f7b9660c7bc56/crates/snes-core/tests/ppu_obj_sizes.rs) and original guests deliberately stay below evaluation limits. Their passes provide no overflow evidence.

These are concrete implementation gaps; the existing loops are not a hardware specification.

## Expected outcome

Implement specification-backed non-interlaced OBJ selection, tile admission and STAT77 overflow reporting, integrated with the existing scanline scheduler. Rendering and status must agree on the admitted objects/tiles.

### Specification prerequisite and hardware contract

Use [Anomie’s Register Doc](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gilligan/snesdev/master/docs/snes_registers.txt), particularly STAT77 and SPRITES, together with [Fullsnes OBJ documentation](https://problemkaputt.de/fullsnes.htm#snesppuspritesobjs) and its status/timing descriptions. The repository’s [Issue #55 specification record](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/a7d944c662b1bbfca3ed9856240f7b9660c7bc56/docs/issue-55-validation.md) identifies Anomie revision 1157 and Fullsnes no$sns v1.5 with SHA-256 hashes.

Before production changes or expected-value construction, record the exact supported rules for:

- The 32-object selection limit and 34 eight-pixel tile limit, including the distinction between reaching and exceeding each limit.
- STAT77 bit 6 RANGE OVER and bit 7 TIME OVER, their accumulation and clearing conditions, repeated-read behavior, and forced-blank interactions.
- Horizontal eligibility during object selection versus tile admission: fully offscreen objects, partially clipped tiles on both edges, and the special encoded X=-256 case.
- Object selection order, tile admission order and within-object tile order, including a stable programmed priority-rotation start and wraparound. Do not assume fetch order equals pixel priority order.
- Whether transparency, overlap, screen routing and windows affect either budget.
- Frame/scanline-zero lifecycle and the relationship between scheduler V coordinates and framebuffer row coordinates.

The raw specification copies referenced by historical validation records are absent from this checkout. This planning inspection therefore does **not** independently establish the unquoted counting, ordering or lifetime details. Resolving those details is a concrete prerequisite within this implementation Issue. Record source sections, versions/hashes, disagreements and derivations; correct any unsupported historical expectation rather than preserving it because a test passed. Clearly distinguish documented hardware rules from scheduler approximations.

### Focused scope and non-goals

Cover static non-interlaced NTSC scenes within the existing 224-row renderer, all current OBSEL dimension pairs, documented evaluation exceptions, overflow lifetime and software-visible status. Preserve Issue #55’s rectangular geometry, flips and character addressing.

Do not add a dot-level fetch pipeline, rendering-time OAM corruption model, arbitrary mid-scanline register effects, complete priority-rotation oddities, interlace, overscan, PAL, enhancement chips or unrelated UI/tooling. Exact physical flag assertion strobes remain unresolved unless supported independently; frame-boundary state must still be implemented and tested.

## Context and reproduction

Construct original scenes under forced blank, enable rendering, then inspect both pixels and CPU reads of `$213E`:

1. Compare 32 and 33 eligible small objects while staying below the tile limit.
2. Compare 34 and 35 admitted tile candidates while staying below the object limit. For example, seventeen 16-pixel-wide objects supply 34 candidate tiles; an additional 8-pixel object supplies the boundary candidate, subject to the confirmed admission rules.
3. Repeat with partial clipping, fully offscreen controls, X=-256, transparent/overlapping objects and distinguishable object/tile identities.

Current `$213E & $C0` is always zero. Pixel survivor expectations must come from the recorded specification contract, not production output.

Inspection was read-only. No tests were rerun and no external specifications were retrieved during planning.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Complete the specification prerequisite above before changing production evaluation or writing expected survivors. Include an explicit selection/admission/lifetime table. Any unresolved physical timing remains labeled and outside the asserted coverage; do not silently substitute an unsupported rule.
- [ ] Implement the confirmed selection and tile budgets, correct survivor ordering, persistent overflow state and scheduler lifecycle. Preserve STAT77’s existing PPU1 open-bus/version behavior and read-bus update path. Reading status must follow the documented flag semantics.
- [ ] Add original Rust tests, runnable with `cargo test --locked -p snes-core --test ppu_obj_limits`, for independent 32/33-object and 34/35-tile boundaries. Assert exact status masks and distinguishable admitted/rejected pixels. Include both-flags and neither-flag controls. Expected results must not call production evaluation helpers or reproduce its loop as an oracle.
- [ ] Cover fully offscreen positions, left/right partial tiles at aligned and unaligned boundaries, X=-256, Y wrapping, transparent and overlapping candidates, disabled OBJ routing/windows, stable rotation with index wraparound, square controls, and selectors 6/7 rectangular controls. Check rectangular lower halves so height and width cannot be conflated.
- [ ] Add natural-scheduler lifecycle tests using ordinary timed accesses: overflow followed by a non-overflow line, repeated status reads, VBlank observation, next-frame clearing and the source-supported forced-blank cases. Do not inject result flags or raster coordinates. Test the chosen scheduler convention without claiming exact physical fetch timing.
- [ ] Add an original source-built CPU guest that initializes OAM/VRAM/CGRAM through registers, reads `$213E`, records independently expected results in WRAM and displays identifiable surviving tiles. Use explicit instruction/frame deadlines. Hosts may load, step and observe; they must not patch guest state. Record MIT provenance, reproducible build commands and generated hashes in `tests/roms/PROVENANCE.md`.
- [ ] Run the new tests against the exact baseline with production unchanged and record behavioral failures separately from build/toolchain failures. Then demonstrate passing results with the implementation.
- [ ] Add a bounded browser check loading the same original guest through the normal ROM picker. Assert CPU-produced status results and literal survivor pixels in actual Wasm framebuffer bytes and canvas ImageData, without host state patches or new debug APIs.
- [ ] Pass `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`, and `cargo test --workspace --locked`. Explicitly retain `ppu_obj_sizes`, `ppu_oam_access`, `ppu_oam_reload`, `ppu_hires`, `ppu_pseudo_hires`, `direct_color`, and OAM unit regressions.
- [ ] Pass the existing [README validation](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/a7d944c662b1bbfca3ed9856240f7b9660c7bc56/README.md#validate) and [CI gates](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/a7d944c662b1bbfca3ed9856240f7b9660c7bc56/.github/workflows/ci.yml): smoke regeneration/comparison; pinned assembler builds; source-built CPU/SPC suites through `tools/hardware-tests.py`; HDMA fixture through `tools/ppu-test.py`; two reproducible cleared-game builds; production Wasm build; and Chromium `npm --prefix web test -- --grep-invert '301 seconds'`. Preserve Castle/Memory source pins, hashes, replays, durations, gameplay/audio assertions and negative controls. Acquire no commercial ROM or firmware.
- [ ] Update README limitations and the validation record with actual commands/results, baseline counterexamples, provenance and remaining uncertainty. Keep all 24 inventory categories and their complete scopes: `cpu`, `bus`, `scheduler`, `dma`, `hdma`, `controllers`, `ppu-bg`, `ppu-offset`, `ppu-hires`, `ppu-mode7`, `ppu-objects`, `ppu-color`, `ppu-ports`, `ppu-raster`, `ppu-display`, `spc`, `ipl`, `dsp-voices`, `dsp-noise`, `dsp-pitch`, `dsp-envelope`, `dsp-echo`, `dsp-timing`, `pal`. This bounded change leaves `ppu-objects` partial; physical evaluation/fetch timing, rotation oddities, interlace and hires interactions remain outstanding. Limited passing tests establish neither full hardware accuracy nor commercial compatibility and do not complete Issue #3.

## Optional validation

Additional independently licensed, source-built OBJ fixtures with explicit provenance. No commercial ROM acquisition or physical-device approval is required.

## Required post-merge verification

None.
